source_title: Vp plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 62 and 63 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised by the Board on 5 June 2019; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 26% to £382.8m, adjusted operating profit increased 17% to £51.6m and adjusted profit before tax grew 15% to £46.8m. Operating margin remained healthy at 13.5%, statutory profit before tax rose to £33.6m and EBITDA increased 20% to £101.4m. Net debt fell to £168.1m despite substantial fleet investment and leverage remained comfortable at 1.7x.
already_announced_exclusion: The Brandon Hire integration and other acquisition-integration activities disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Strong revenue, profit and cash growth, falling debt and comfortable leverage provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence, with no material forward restructuring pressure beyond already-disclosed integration.

source_title: Vp plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 71 and 72 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised by the Board on 8 June 2021; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue fell 15% to £308.0m, adjusted operating profit nearly halved to £27.7m, adjusted margin contracted to 9.0% from 14.3% and adjusted profit before tax fell to £23.3m from £47.1m. Exceptional and impairment charges contributed to a £2.3m statutory loss before tax. However, trading recovered to 95% of the prior-year run rate, net debt fell £37.9m to £121.9m and the Group remained within covenants.
already_announced_exclusion: The Covid-driven cost reductions, mothballed or reopened locations, restructuring programme, furlough actions and Hire Station goodwill impairment disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The revenue and profit collapse, margin compression and statutory loss create very high pressure. Strong late-year recovery, material debt reduction and covenant compliance provide meaningful contrary evidence.

source_title: Vp plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 87 and 90 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised by the Board on 6 June 2023; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 6% to £371.5m, adjusted profit before tax increased 4% to approximately £40.5m, adjusted EBITDA rose to £92.9m and adjusted earnings per share grew to 79.0p. Adjusted margin eased to 10.8% from 11.1%, statutory profit before tax fell to £30.7m and net debt excluding leases rose modestly to £134.4m. Return on capital employed remained strong at 14.4%.
already_announced_exclusion: The terminated formal sale process, £3.3m restructuring costs and depot closures across three business units disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Modest statutory profit and margin weakness and slightly higher debt create limited pressure. Revenue, adjusted profit and EBITDA growth, strong returns and a healthy balance sheet provide very strong contrary evidence.
